s1.syndrome_frame: Complex multisystem disorder with cardiac and gastrointestinal involvement
salient_findings: Heart murmur in right heart region
Elevated liver enzymes and total bile acid
key_facts: Hepatomegaly and increased radiopacity in upper right abdomen
Liver enlargement and gallbladder mucocele-like findings on ultrasound
Renal cysts and enlarged adrenal glands

raw.syndrome_frame: Complex multisystem disorder with cardiac and gastrointestinal involvement
salient_findings: Heart murmur in right heart region
Elevated liver enzymes and total bile acid
key_facts: Hepatomegaly and increased radiopacity in upper right abdomen
Liver enlargement and gallbladder mucocele-like findings on ultrasound
Renal cysts and enlarged adrenal glands

shortlist.label: Congestive heart failure
shortlist.why_kept: Previous diagnosis of tricuspid regurgitation and current heart murmur

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hepatomegaly, liver enlargement, and elevated liver enzymes

raw.rationale: The dog's previous diagnosis of tricuspid regurgitation, elevated heart rate, and enlarged cardiac silhouette on thoracic radiography support this diagnosis. Additionally, the presence of hepatomegaly and increased radiopacity in the upper right abdomen can be secondary to congestive heart failure.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: While the dog has elevated liver enzymes and hepatomegaly, there is no direct evidence of a liver tumor.

rejected.label: Gallbladder mucocele
rejected.why: Although the dog has gallbladder mucocele-like findings on ultrasound, this is not the primary diagnosis that explains the majority of the clinical signs.

rejected.label: Renal cystic disease
rejected.why: The presence of renal cysts is noted, but it is not the primary diagnosis that explains the dog's clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Intestinal parasitism
rejected.why: While the dog has parasites in its stool, this is not the primary diagnosis that explains the majority of the clinical signs, including the cardiac and hepatic abnormalities.
